sections.heading: Praising you for who you are
sections.text: Most High God, you made the earth from end to end, and nothing in the universe is outside your rule. You judge every person with perfect justice, you lead and care for your church, and you save sinners like us. Your greatness is beyond what we can measure. Your goodness has no limit. Your compassion does not run out. Your care reaches farther than we can see, and your mercy is new for us again today.
theological_themes: God is Creator, ruler, judge, head of the church, and Savior; his mercy and providence are inexhaustible.

scripture_references.connection: This passage presents God as the everlasting Creator whose understanding cannot be searched out, grounding the prayer’s praise of his greatness and care over all creation.
The passage speaks of the Lord’s steadfast love and mercy as unfailing and renewed, directly supporting the prayer’s confidence that God’s compassion does not run dry.
Paul describes Christ as given as head over all things to the church, which supports the prayer’s confession that God rules and cares for his people through Christ.

sections.heading: Thanking you for the gospel you have spoken to us
sections.text: Father, thank you for giving us the message of salvation. The gospel is not a small or distant thing to us. It tells us what is true, gives us promises we can lean on, and invites us to come to you in peace. We need exactly this good news: we are lost, and you offer us a salvation that is complete, free, and everlasting. We are weak, and you point us to the strong Savior. We are poor, and in him we find riches we could never earn. We are blind, and in him are wisdom and knowledge that open our eyes.
theological_themes: The gospel addresses human need with God’s full and gracious salvation in Christ.

scripture_references.connection: Paul calls the gospel God’s power for salvation and says it reveals righteousness from God, which supports the prayer’s gratitude for the gospel as the saving message we depend on.
Jesus describes his mission as seeking and saving the lost, matching the prayer’s confession that our lostness is answered by God’s salvation in Christ.
This passage locates the treasures of wisdom and knowledge in Christ, supporting the prayer’s claim that our blindness and poverty are met in him.

sections.heading: Receiving your greatest gift: your Son
sections.text: Thank you for the gift we could never deserve or fully describe: your Son. Jesus is our only safe place, our foundation, our hope, and our confidence before you. We are not trusting our goodness, our effort, or our record. We depend on his death for us. We rest in the righteousness that is ours in him. Make us more like him, not just in what we say, but in what we love, choose, and do.
theological_themes: Christ alone is the believer’s refuge, foundation, righteousness, and hope; salvation rests on his death and righteousness, not our merit.

scripture_references.connection: Paul’s thanksgiving for God’s inexpressible gift fits the prayer’s gratitude for the Son as the gift beyond our deserving or full comprehension.
Paul says no foundation can be laid other than Jesus Christ, grounding the prayer’s confession that Christ is the only foundation for our confidence.
This passage explains the exchange at the heart of the gospel: Christ bears sin so that believers become righteous in him, supporting the prayer’s dependence on his death and righteousness.
Paul teaches that God’s saving purpose includes conforming believers to the image of his Son, which supports the request to bear Christ’s likeness.

sections.heading: Asking that Christ would fill our hearts
sections.text: Let Jesus be large in our minds today. Let his beauty, worth, and glory shape what we think about. Let his love have the deepest place in our affections, so that lesser loves do not rule us. Let his cross stir us out of coldness and make us eager to live for him with steady, grateful devotion.
theological_themes: The glory, love, and cross of Christ should reshape the believer’s thoughts, loves, and zeal.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says Christ’s love controls believers because he died for them, so they no longer live for themselves; this grounds the prayer’s desire for Christ’s love and cross to direct our lives.

Paul connects the believer’s daily life to union with the crucified and risen Christ, especially Christ’s personal love and self-giving, supporting the prayer’s longing for devotion shaped by the cross.

sections.heading: Living faithfully where you have placed us
sections.text: As Christians, help us to live faithfully in the different places you have put us. Keep us from the traps that come with our roles, responsibilities, relationships, work, comforts, and pressures. Help us do the duties that belong to our circumstances without resentment or pride. Teach us to enjoy your gifts with self-control, to use our opportunities diligently, and to be useful wherever we are. Let every home, workplace, church, friendship, and conversation be better because we are there as people who belong to Christ.
theological_themes: Christian faithfulness is lived out in ordinary circumstances through holiness, duty, moderation, service, and love for others.

scripture_references.connection: Paul calls believers to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, which supports the prayer’s desire to live faithfully in every role and situation.
Paul teaches believers to live faithfully in the life circumstances assigned to them by the Lord, grounding the prayer’s concern for obedience in our actual callings and responsibilities.
Peter urges believers to use their gifts to serve others as stewards of God’s grace, supporting the prayer’s request to be useful and beneficial in every place and company.
Paul instructs those with advantages to avoid arrogance, hope in God, and be rich in good works, which supports the prayer’s desire to enjoy benefits moderately and use them diligently.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original phrase about filling our “various situations in life” can sound like acceptance of fixed social rank or unjust circumstances. This adaptation renders it as faithfulness within roles, responsibilities, relationships, work, comforts, and pressures, without implying that every social arrangement is morally right.
The prayer’s reliance on Christ’s death and righteousness reflects a classic Protestant understanding of atonement and justification. That theology is preserved rather than softened.
significant_interpretive_choices: “Words of salvation” was interpreted as the gospel message in its doctrines, promises, and invitations, not merely Scripture in general.
“Help is found in One that is mighty” was rendered as looking to the strong Savior, identifying the helper as Christ in keeping with the surrounding gospel focus.
“Rest in his righteousness” was rendered as trusting the righteousness that is ours in Christ, to preserve the original’s emphasis on confidence before God grounded outside ourselves.
“His cross inflame us with ardour” was expressed as the cross stirring us out of coldness into grateful devotion, preserving zeal while avoiding archaic emotional language.
